title: Browne Trading Company
about: Rod Browne Mitchell’s family has fished Maine’s Kennebec River and Merrymeeting Bay since the early 1700s. In the early 1980s he ran a wine and cheese shop in Camden. Then the chef Jean-Louis Palladin asked him to find the Maine seafood other suppliers overlooked, such as scallops and elvers, and introduced him to a caviar source. In 1991 Mitchell opened Browne Trading Company on Portland’s working waterfront, and it now supplies many of the country’s leading kitchens.

Browne sells fresh fish and shellfish, smoked seafood from its own smokehouse, and a wide range of caviar, from American roes to osetra. The company builds its sourcing on transparency and traceability, and it tells customers where and how each fish was caught or raised so they can buy without harming the future health of the oceans.
Its market is at 262 Commercial Street in Portland’s historic fishing district. The retail shop opened in 2000 and also sells wine, cheese and a smoked-salmon lunch.
